title: Nanodisc Single-Molecule Pull-Down Assay for Protein-Lipid Interactions
author: Reyes-Ordoñez, Shree, et al.

steps.title: Drill holes in quartz slide
steps.instruction: Using a drill, make evenly spaced holes along the long edges of each quartz slide; each hole should be ~0.75 mm in diameter and positioned 3–4 mm from the edge.

steps.title: Clean slides by sonication and torch
steps.instruction: Place slides and coverslips in a glass Coplin jar and sonicate sequentially: ultrapure water 10 min, methanol 10 min, acetone 10 min, ultrapure water 2 min, methanol 10 min, ultrapure water 1 min. Burn each slide with a propane torch for ≥1 min until residues disappear. Return slides to the jar and sonicate in 1:1 HCl:methanol for 30 min, then methanol for 2 min, rinsing with the next solvent after each sonication step.

steps.title: Activate slide surface
steps.instruction: Sonicate slides in 2 M KOH for 30 min. Immediately add 1.5 mL aminosilane to a mixture of 100 mL methanol + 4 mL acetic acid, pour into the jar, incubate in the dark 10 min at room temperature (22‑24 °C). Sonicate 1 min, then keep in the dark another 10 min.

steps.title: Passivate surface with PEG
steps.instruction: For each slide/coverslip pair, dissolve 23 mg mPEG and 0.7 mg biotin‑PEG in 100 µL freshly prepared 10 mM sodium bicarbonate (pH 8.5); spin 30 s at 10,000 g (22‑24 °C) to remove bubbles. Apply the 100 µL PEG solution to one side of the slide, spread evenly by tilting, and immediately cover with a cleaned coverslip. Incubate in a humidified, light‑protected chamber 3–4 h (up to 24 h) at 22‑24 °C. Label the un‑PEGylated side, separate the pair, rinse the entire slide with ~500 mL ultrapure water, blow‑dry with N₂, place each pair in a 50‑mL conical tube, seal with a food‑grade vacuum sealer, and store at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare lipid mixture for nanodiscs
steps.instruction: In a glass tube, combine lipids dissolved in chloroform: 1.069 µmol DMPC, 0.214 µmol DMPS, 0.142 µmol PIP (total lipid‑to‑protein molar ratio 95:1). Dry the mixture slowly under a N₂ stream while rotating the tube at an angle to form a thin uniform film. Place the tube in a vacuum desiccator for 4 h–24 h at 22‑24 °C.

steps.title: Reconstitute lipids and assemble nanodiscs
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL reconstitution buffer (20 mM Tris‑Cl, 100 mM NaCl, pH 7.4) to the dried lipids, then add sodium cholate (0.2 M stock) to reach a final cholate concentration of 12–40 mM (max 40 mM). Vortex, warm the tube in ~55 °C tap water for a few minutes, then sonicate in a bath sonicator until the solution is clear (30 s–2 min). Add 0.015 µmol MSP1D1, incubate 15 min at 22‑24 °C.

steps.title: Remove detergent with Amberlite beads
steps.instruction: Transfer the lipid‑protein mixture to a microtube containing 100‑150 µL pre‑soaked Amberlite XAD‑2 beads (soaked in distilled water). Incubate on an orbital shaker 2 h (up to 24 h) at 22‑24 °C. Centrifuge 1 min at 500‑1,000 g, collect the supernatant, pass it through a 0.2‑µm bio‑inert membrane to remove residual beads, and store the clarified nanodisc solution at 4 °C until further use.

steps.title: Purify nanodiscs by size‑exclusion chromatography
steps.instruction: Run the nanodisc sample on a Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL column equilibrated with degassed PBS (pH 7.4) at 0.75 mL/min, collecting 0.375 mL fractions. Combine fractions that contain the pure nanodisc peak (identified by the protein absorbance). Measure A₂₈₀; calculate [MSP1D1] = A₂₈₀/(23,950 × path length cm) and [Nanodisc] = [MSP1D1]/2. Typical concentration ≈7.5 µM.

steps.title: Store nanodiscs
steps.instruction: For short‑term use, keep at 4 °C for 2–3 weeks. For long‑term storage, add 15‑20 % (v/v) of an 80 % glycerol solution, aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂, and store at –80 °C. Before reuse, thaw and repeat the SEC purification (step 8); concentration will be lower.

steps.title: Label nanodiscs with DiD
steps.instruction: Mix DiD (1,1′‑dioctadecyl‑3,3,3′,3′‑tetramethylindodicarbocyanine) with the nanodisc stock at a 10:1 molar ratio (DiD:Nanodisc). Incubate 1–1.5 h at 37 °C. Store the labeled nanodiscs at 4 °C and use within 2–3 weeks.

steps.title: Construct slide chambers
steps.instruction: Cut narrow strips of double‑sided tape with a sharp blade and place them on the passivated side of a slide; the spacing between strips (the chamber width) must be ≥5 mm. Lay a coverslip (passivated side down) on top, press gently with a pipet tip to ensure tight adhesion. Apply a thin line of fast‑drying epoxy along both edges of each chamber (avoiding the sample‑loading holes) and let it cure completely.

steps.title: Add neutrAvidin to chambers
steps.instruction: Prepare a 200 µg/mL neutrAvidin solution in T50 buffer. Flow 60 µL of this solution into each chamber, incubate 10 min at 22‑24 °C, then proceed.

steps.title: Immobilize DiD‑nanodiscs on slide
steps.instruction: Dilute the DiD‑labeled nanodisc stock 100‑fold in T50 buffer (initial dilution). Flow 80 µL of the diluted nanodiscs into a chamber, incubate 10 min, then flow 80 µL T50 buffer to wash away unbound discs.

steps.title: Optimize nanodisc surface density
steps.instruction: Image the chamber on a TIRF microscope in the DiD channel (638 nm) using 20‑frame movies at 10 fps. Count immobilized discs; aim for 550‑750 counts per field. If counts are low, prepare a higher‑concentration nanodisc dilution and repeat the flow‑wash step; if counts are high, dilute further and repeat. Once the optimal count is achieved, acquire 10 such images. Then switch to the GFP channel (488 nm) and acquire 20‑frame movies at 10 fps in at least 10 different areas per chamber for background reference.

steps.title: Prepare cell lysates
steps.instruction: Wash transfected HEK293 cells once with ice‑cold PBS. Add 300 µL detergent‑free buffer (DFB) containing freshly added protease‑inhibitor cocktail (PIC) to the cells, keep on ice 1‑2 min, scrape with a cell scraper, and transfer the suspension to a microcentrifuge tube. Lyse by passing the suspension through a 26‑gauge needle 15‑20 times (or by brief probe sonication, 3‑5 s).

steps.title: Clarify lysates
steps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge the lysate at 90,500 g for 30 min at 4 °C using tubes rated for such speeds. Transfer the cleared supernatant to a fresh tube, keep on ice, and use within 1 h.

steps.title: Determine eGFP concentration in lysate
steps.instruction: In a black 96‑well plate, add 50 µL PBS to each well. Add 50 µL cleared lysate to the test wells (mix gently, avoid bubbles). Prepare eGFP standards (1, 5, 15, 50, 100, 350, 700 nM) in DFB, add 50 µL standard + 50 µL PBS to separate wells. Measure fluorescence at 488 nm with a plate reader, generate a standard curve from the pure eGFP wells, and calculate the eGFP concentration in the lysate samples.

steps.title: Process raw image files
steps.instruction: For each acquisition, locate the .log and .pma files. Run the publicly available IDL script package (ana_all.pro) to perform PSF fitting; this generates .pks (particle list), .trace (intensity vs time), and two .tif images (average projection with/without detected spots).

steps.title: Count GFP spots in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Import the .pks files into MATLAB and run the Count_gfp_spots.m script to obtain spot counts per field. The assay readout is the average difference in GFP spot count between ‘after lysate addition’ and ‘before lysate addition’ images.

steps.title: Set binding threshold
steps.instruction: Gather GFP‑spot‑count data from >100 negative‑control assays (e.g., nanodiscs lacking PIP or using a non‑binding protein). Compute the mean and standard deviation; define the binding threshold as mean + 2 × SD (example threshold ≈80 counts). Any assay exceeding this value is considered positive for binding.

steps.title: Photobleaching step analysis
steps.instruction: Run the ana_all_brief IDL script for background subtraction and Gaussian fitting. Import the output into MATLAB. Use view_traces_New to visualize each trace and set background levels. Run distribution_CKfilt to separate traces into GFP‑only, DiD‑only, and both‑signal groups. Apply Chung‑Kennedy filtration to smooth the ‘both’ traces and generate PNG images of each trace. Manually classify the number of photobleaching steps in the GFP signal of each trace (reference monomeric and tandem‑dimer GFP controls). Note that blurry movies or overly dense fields can inflate multi‑step counts.

steps.title: Dwell‑time analysis
steps.instruction: From the same processed data, select traces showing transient binding events (re‑binding on the same spot). Use the Transient_dwell MATLAB script to measure dwell times, excluding fluorescence immediately after the 488 nm excitation pulse. Fit the dwell‑time distribution with an exponential decay model (maximum‑likelihood estimation) to obtain the dissociation rate constant (k_off); calculate SEM and 95 % confidence intervals.
